thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: SEV2 page: streaming p99 latency spike detected in us-west-2 (proxy clusters). AlertID=INC-2026-3429. auto-escalate in 5m if not acked

oncall-sre-erin: Acked. I'm on it. What are we seeing?

matt: seeing p95 jump from ~180ms -> 1.2s and p99 ~4.8s on streaming responses. SSE and websocket tail latency. Charts: https://grafana.redwood/streams/us-west-2 (link)

nina: Confirming increase in stalled chunk counts on proxy nginx-streamer shards 7/8. queuesize metric spiking. client-backpressure events also up.

platform-kai: tagging: looks like downstream upstream-workers have a backlog on recv buffer. Kernel TCP queuems > 500ms on some hosts. Also seeing many KEEPALIVE timeouts from proxies to clients.

infra-anita: rolling logs show repeated 504s from proxy to edge: 
```
[2026-03-15T12:46:02Z] proxy/nginx-streamer-7 upstream timed out (110: Connection timed out) while reading response header from upstream
```

cs-lee: two customers reported partial streams (clients see long pauses and then final chunk). One is a high-throughput customer on dedicated capacity. They just paged CS.

oncall-sre-erin: quick impact estimate: p99 spike across streaming endpoints for last 12m. Approx 3.4% of streaming requests experienced stalls >2s. Not complete failures, but user-visible jitter and some reconnects. Marking PII? No.

matt: digging into tail traces. The requests that stall share pattern: long-lived SSE with periodic small chunks. Chunk rate slowed then pause for 3-10s, then burst. Likely proxy buffer fill + client stalled read.

proxy-bot: note: rate-limited clients are showing TCP RCV buffer fill and zero window events. Recommending look into NGINX proxy_send_timeout and proxy_buffering settings.

nina: I can reproduce on staging with heavy connection fanout. When I throttle client read rate, nginx buffers until proxy_buffer_size threshold then backpressures upstream causing worker stalls.

platform-kai: candidate root causes: 1) a recent config change to proxy-buffering limits rolled yesterday (smaller buffers), 2) a kernel patch that changed tcp_autotune on some hosts, or 3) a surge of clients with very slow readers causing head-of-line blocking.

oncall-sre-erin: immediate mitigations to reduce customer impact:
- lower keepalive timeout between proxy and clients (reduce half-open lingering)
- increase proxy buffering threshold for streaming endpoints to avoid frequent backpressure signals
- enable graceful downscaling: route traffic to hotspot-avoiding pool (dedicated capacity or different AZ)
- temporary rate-limit slow-consumer connections at edge (drop after X seconds of zero-window)

matt: I'm going to bump nginx proxy_buffer_size on the streaming vhost from 8k -> 64k and increase proxy_buffers. Pushing change to canary shard now.

platform-kai: I'll push a kernel rollback on the two affected hosts if canary suggests it's kernel-related.

infra-anita: I can gate a config change via deploy bot. matt, please post the exact command/config snippet you plan to apply.

matt: applying via runbook: 
```
# canary patch
kubectl -n proxy set configmap nginx-streaming-config \
  --from-literal=proxy_buffer_size=64k \
  --from-literal=proxy_buffers="8 64k"
kubectl rollout restart deployment/nginx-streamer-canary
```

matt: canary applied to shard-7. Observing metrics...

5m later

matt: canary shard metrics show p95 down from 1.2s -> 260ms, p99 down from 4.8s -> 900ms. No increase in memory OOM on canary.

nina: client zero-window events decreased on canary by ~70%. This suggests proxy buffering was the main trigger.

oncall-sre-erin: roll to remaining shards but do it gradually with 2 shard concurrency to avoid sudden memory pressure. Also enable an alert for proxy_buffer_fill to catch regressions.

platform-kai: rolling to rest of prod shards now. Will also add temporary iptables rule to drop persistently zero-window clients after 20s to limit head-of-line.

cs-lee: updated impacted customers with note that we've applied a mitigaiton and monitoring. Offered follow-up postmortem. Customer wants ETA on root cause and whether they'll need config changes on their side.

matt: full roll complete. Aggregate p95 ~220ms, p99 ~500-600ms across us-west-2. Stalled chunk counts back to baseline.

oncall-sre-erin: monitoring for 30m. Collecting traces for later RCA: - request ids, affected connection ids, proxy shard ids, kernel settings. If numbers re-spike, we'll escalate to SEV1.

proxy-bot: automated note: deployed config change nginx-streaming-config@v2026-03-15T12:58Z by matt.

infra-anita: followups: schedule change revert test in staging to validate whether kernel change contributes. Also will run a controlled slow-client stress test against canary to reproduce.

platform-kai: followups: consider soft-LRU or streaming-aware buffer policy so one slow client doesn't degrade entire proxy. Long-term design action item: streaming sharding per-client-size.

cs-lee: created customer update ticket CS-8123 and flagged account team.

oncall-sre-erin: summary for handoff: Issue: streaming tail latency spikes caused by proxy_buffering config + slow-client zero-window events causing upstream backpressure -> p95/p99 SLO breaches. Mitigation: increased proxy buffer size and rolled config across shards; traffic routing and client drop rule applied. Impact: ~3.4% requests experience stalls >2s window for ~15m; no data loss; some reconnects and degraded UX. Next actions: RCA (root cause: confirm config vs kernel), design work on streaming-aware buffering, customer follow-ups.

oncall-sre-erin: handing off to next oncall (matt) for watch window 30m. Please escalate if p99 >1s for >5m.

matt: taking watch. ping me in #incidents if anything odd. :thumbsup:

cs-lee: marking customers notified and scheduling postmortem walk-through for 16:00 PST.

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-3429 status -> mitigated. Timeline and notes will be published to the incident page. :white_check_mark:
